decision: block the proposed reserve-first policy pending a wake/close design and deterministic native validation

findings.name: normal rejected reservation can strand shutdown
interleaving: Q=1 and the actor is waiting in blocking_recv with an empty channel
producer passes stopped/length checks and obtains the sole try_reserve permit
shutdown sets stopping, try_send(Stop) returns Full, and shutdown awaits actor join
producer discovers over-budget capacity or aggregate byte pressure, returns and drops its unsent permit
the permit is returned but its Drop does not wake the receiver while the semaphore is open; no command reaches blocking_recv and the stop flag is checked only after a receive
findings.consequence: The actor and shutdown can remain blocked indefinitely even after producer returns. Other new requests see stopping and cannot supply a wake. This is a source-derived interleaving, not a native execution.

findings.name: post-close reserved send may retain a job and oneshot
interleaving: Q>=2 and producer holds a reserved slot
shutdown sends Stop through another slot; actor exits and drops the receiver
producer uses the previously reserved Tokio permit to send its request after receiver drop
findings.consequence: Tokio documents Permit::send succeeds after close; inspected Rx::drop drains before this later send and Chan::drop performs final drain only when channel owners disappear. The job may retain its response sender and byte charge while ControllerHandler still owns a sender, leaving direct submit awaiting without a local deadline. This static conclusion needs a deterministic native control.

findings.name: byte pressure closes transport and has no fair admission
findings.detail: Transport maps Handler errors to HandlerError and closes the connection; remote callers do not receive a retryable Busy body. Immediate slot/byte checks permit starvation of larger individually valid jobs by smaller repeated admissions. The proposed policy changes valid-success behavior and can introduce these failures even with a free queue slot.

required_followup: Choose and specify a reliable actor wake/close mechanism that handles rejected/panicking reservations, shutdown cancellation and receiver-drop races; a simple stopping-flag recheck is insufficient.

Consider an atomic byte reservation before the existing try_send, with explicitly documented non-racing error precedence and race semantics, or a separately owned shutdown signal; do not claim either safe without review.
Add deterministic Q=1 reserve/stop/reject and Q>=2 reserve/receiver-drop/send tests, bound their waits and ensure failed tests explicitly wake/join the actor rather than leaking a blocking task.
Prove exactly-once byte-charge release on failed admission, canceled receiver, actor dequeue/stop and channel destruction, without charging active/replied allocations to the queue bound.

Test direct Handler and transport behavior, original buffers, no-copy pointer identities, full/closed/oversized error precedence, contention and starvation properties; preserve existing assertions and deadlines.
limits: Static source and sequential model review only; no Rust compilation, Cargo, Tokio execution, actor/WAL or network test.
The existing B=Q*L counter proposal is explicitly a queued logical-capacity estimate, not a total-process or active/reply bound.
No throughput, production-readiness or release-readiness conclusion.
